why_relevant: Leading Ukrainian economic daily; publishes bankers' and market reaction pieces on NBU rule changes and is frequently first with political context around draft laws affecting payments (interchange, cash limits, taxation of card transfers).

Tech-startup outlet that covers fintech licensing, NBU restrictions on crypto/e-wallet players and product-level consequences of payment rules; complements finance-desk outlets with a builder/startup perspective on compliance deadlines.

Banking trade portal; ran a dedicated explainer on the 'summer wave' of NBU regulation bundling open banking, acquiring rules and interchange regulation into one deadline calendar — exactly the deadline-clustering signal this workstream needs.

Niche banking-supervision specialist outlet; covers NBU internal organisation (e.g. reorganisation of the Banking Supervision Department) and supervisory practice — signals that rarely reach mainstream media but shape enforcement capacity and timing.
Mainstream business desk with dated 'what changes from <date>' explainers on payment-service rules; good for confirming effective dates and for lay-language framing of NBU resolutions.

High-volume news agency-style outlet; publishes fast 'what changes for banks, business and clients' pieces on NBU financial-monitoring rule updates, useful as a corroboration/timing layer rather than a primary analytical source.
Legal-profession outlet that reads NBU resolutions as legal texts and explains who is obliged, from when, and with what sanctions — bridges trade press and primary regulation.
Consumer-finance portal aggregating banking/credit/deposit news; secondary corroboration layer and a pointer to smaller Ukrainian finance outlets it republishes.

Ukraine's dominant news aggregator exposes a stable per-source feed page for each outlet, giving a low-friction, bot-tolerant way to monitor niche finance outlets (like FINBALANCE) whose own sites may lack RSS. Also a discovery surface for further Ukrainian finance outlets.

Community/association channel of the Ukrainian fintech community; functions as a de-facto specialist newsletter — posts NBU consultation openings, deadline reminders and practitioner complaints faster than editorial media. The /s/ web-preview endpoint is publicly readable without an account.

AML/fin-monitoring software vendor publishing dated explainers on NBU limit changes (e.g. card-to-card transfer limits from 1 June). Vendor content is biased toward selling compliance, which makes it an early and detailed indicator of what obligations firms must implement and by when.

English-language Ukrainian outlet republishing Interfax-Ukraine economic dispatches; usable free English proxy for wire content and for how Ukrainian financial regulation is framed to foreign investors.

International payments trade publication that picks up Ukrainian NBU open-banking and payment-rule changes for a global audience; useful English cross-check and for spotting which Ukrainian changes matter to foreign PSPs.

Established Ukrainian business publication (part of a media bureau with mmr.ua/womo.ua); carries banking and regulatory reporting. Included as a secondary trade-press candidate — no regulation-specific article was surfaced in this run, so relevance is inferred from the outlet's beat.

source_name: NBU News feed (bank.gov.ua) — speeches, interviews and press briefings of Governor and Deputy Governors
why_relevant: Primary publication channel for NBU officials' speeches ('Виступ...'), interviews ('Інтерв'ю...') and press-briefing transcripts. Deputy-Governor speeches routinely pre-announce regulatory direction (e.g. Serhii Kholod on 'conceptual changes in regulating the Ukrainian payment market' / PSD2 transposition) months before a draft act exists. Titles are formulaic, making automated filtering of speech/interview items reliable.

source_name: NBU News (English) — speeches and briefings mirror
why_relevant: English mirror of the same speech/interview stream. Useful for cross-checking terminology of forthcoming rules (PSD2, open banking, prudential requirements) and for items aimed at international audiences (e.g. NBU First Deputy Governor Serhiy Nikolaychuk keynote at AFME European Financial Integration Conference 2026, Frankfurt).

source_name: NBU monetary policy / publications calendar (Графік засідань і основних публікацій)
why_relevant: Forward calendar of Board meetings and press briefings — gives the exact dates on which forward-looking commentary will be delivered, so a collector can pre-schedule capture rather than discover after the fact. Deadline-relevant for A3.

source_name: NBU official YouTube channel — press briefings and conference appearances (video)
why_relevant: Press briefings are streamed in full; Q&A after the prepared statement is where officials give unscripted timelines for forthcoming rules that never reach the written release. Highest-yield weak-signal medium in this cell.

source_name: NABU event pages — Fintech & Payments Forum 2026 (agenda + speaker list)
why_relevant: Conference agendas are the cell's core artefact: session titles name the exact rule topics under negotiation and the panel lists name the officials who own them, giving both the topic and the person to watch.

The older/rival banking association (claims ~125 member banks), works with the Verkhovna Rada on banking legislation and with the NBU on regulatory support. Organiser of FinTech Ukraine Forum (2026 edition held 29 May, Kyiv) — explicitly framed as a regulator/government/industry dialogue platform on EU-integration-driven market transformation. Its legislative angle complements NBU-centric sources.

source_name: FinTech Ukraine Forum 2026 — press release / agenda coverage (Interfax-Ukraine press-release wire)
why_relevant: Organiser-issued press release describing the 2026 forum (AUB-organised, Kyiv, 29 May) with the framing 'євроінтеграція, цифровізація та ШІ у фокусі' — names the regulatory themes and the regulator/government participants. Interfax's press-release channel is a general pointer to Ukrainian financial-event announcements, not just this one.

source_name: Ukrainian Financial Forum (UFF), organised by ICU
why_relevant: Long-running flagship annual forum (named in the cell brief) bringing together NBU leadership, government and investors; historical archives (e.g. uff.icu/uff-2021/) preserve past programmes, which is useful for learning which rule topics were previewed how far ahead of adoption — a calibration dataset for lead-time estimation.

source_name: Українська асоціація фінтех та інноваційних компаній (UAFIC / FinTech Ukraine)
why_relevant: The fintech industry body named in the cell brief. Acts as a hub between fintechs, banks, and government agencies and runs Ukraine's largest annual fintech conference UAFIN.TECH plus Ukraine Fintech Week and Digital Lending. Its positions and event agendas surface payment/lending rule changes early, and it is a standing counterparty in NBU consultations.

Ukraine's largest fintech conference; NBU speakers recur (e.g. Andriy Podderiogin, Director of the NBU Department of Payment Systems and Innovation Development — the exact official who owns forthcoming payment rules). Agenda + speaker list yields a directly actionable actor map for A3.

source_name: Ukraine Fintech Week — recap and speaker coverage (Scroll.media)
why_relevant: Event recaps are the practical substitute for missing transcripts: they report what NBU/IMF/World Bank speakers actually said on stage, including forward-looking regulatory statements that appear nowhere in official releases.

source_name: Фінансовий клуб (Financial Club) — round tables, online broadcasts and special projects
why_relevant: Since 2009 runs the recurring closed-ish round tables where NBU officials and bank CEOs debate the coming year's regulatory requirements (e.g. the 20 January 'Banking sector of Ukraine: 2025 achievements and 2026 expectations' online broadcast covering capital, liquidity and regulatory requirements). Video/photo archives make these recoverable after the fact.

source_name: Міжнародний фінансовий клуб «БАНКIР» (International Financial Club BANKIR) — banking forums
why_relevant: Long-running Kyiv forum organiser (Banking Forum: Digital Trends; Digital Banking Ecosystem & Fintech, held 12 Aug 2026). Publishes per-event programme and speakers pages, including archived programmes going back years — a reliable, structured agenda source with named regulator speakers.

source_name: European Business Association (EBA Ukraine) — events and financial-services committee readouts
why_relevant: Runs closed-door meetings between the NBU top management and business (e.g. Deputy Governor Yuriy Heletiy and the NBU team with the Currency Regulation and Financial Services Committee on easing FX restrictions). Readouts of these sessions preview liberalisation and regulatory sequencing well before formal acts — a distinct channel from bank-only associations because it carries the corporate/foreign-investor demand side.
